BIRLA INSTITUTE OF TECHNOLOGY, MESRA, RANCHI
(MID SEMESTER EXAMINATION)

CLASS: BE   SEMESTER: VI
BRANCH: IT   SESSION : SP/2019

SUBJECT: IT6025-INFORMATION & CODING THEORY

TIME: 1.5  HOURS   FULL MARKS: 25

INSTRUCTIONS:
1. The total marks of the questions are 30.
2. Candidates may attempt for all 30 marks.
3. In those cases where the marks obtained exceed 25 marks, the excess will be ignored.
4. Before attempting the question paper, be sure that you have got the correct question paper.
5. The missing data, if any, may be assumed suitably.
----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------


Q1 (a) State  Kraft’s  inequality  and  using  it  state  if  an  instantaneous  code  of  codeword
lengths 2, 3, 3, 4, 4 can be created. If yes, what would the codewords be? Assume
the alphabet set X= {0,1}.
[2]
 (b) Compute the Discrete Cosine Transform coefficients given f(x) = {2, 2 4, 6}.  [3]

Q2 (a) What is the difference between source encoding and channel encoding? [2]
 (b) A coin is tossed repeatedly. The coin is unfair and P(H)=p. The game ends the first time
that two consecutive heads (HH) or two consecutive tails (TT) are observed. The player
wins if HH is observed and loses if TT is observed. Find the probability that the player
wins.
[3]



Q3 (a) Describe the features of a Binary Symmetric Channel. [2]
 (b) Let X = {0, 1} and consider two distributions p and q on X. Let p (0) = 1 − r, p (1) = r,
and let q (0) = 1 − s, q (1) = s. Calculate Kullback–Leibler distance between p(x) and
q(x) when i) r=s, ii) r=1/2, s=1/4.
[3]

Q4 (a) Compute the codewords generated by using Huffman coding for each of the following
symbols using their probability of occurrence. P(a)= 1, P(b)= 1, P(c)= 3, P(d)= 4, P(e)=
4, P(f)= 6, P(g)= 9, P(h)= 10.
[2]
 (b) Using the Huffman tree generated in above question, find the new codewords of each
symbol using Adaptive Huffman encoding technique given that the following symbols
are received: ‘acde’.
[3]

Q5 (a) Using concept of N
th
 extension of source, prove whether the following code in uniquely
decodable or not. a-0; b-11; c-00; d-01.
[2]
 (b) In a bag there are 6 Red balls, 9 Green balls, 5 Blue balls and 8 Yellow balls. A ball is
chosen randomly from the bag and kept back into the bag. 6 times balls are chosen in
this manner. Explain, in how many minimum numbers of binary questions can one guess
which 6 balls were chosen?
[3]



Q6 (a) State and explain the relationship between entropy and mutual information. [2]
 (b) Compute the input sequence from alphabet set S= {a, b, c, d} corresponding to the Tag
value= 0.605275, using Arithmetic decoding technique, given that p(a)= 0.25, p(b)=
0.45, p(c)= 0.1, p(d)= 0.2.
[3]
